summary: The tool bar now ends with a Hand, after Measure, as the UI design mock draws it. Pick it and dragging the canvas moves the view instead of moving or picking anything, so a mouse can pan a zoomed picture for the first time.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/design-mode-tool-strip-walk.json.

try.do: Open a new window, pick the Design UI tile and press New UI canvas.
Zoom in until the screen is bigger than the window (pinch, or Command +).
Click the hand at the right end of the tool bar.
Press on the Login screen and drag right and down.
Let go and press V: the screen is still where you placed it, only the view moved.
Show Everything from the mode menu: the Hand is the last button on the bar there too.

evaluate: Does the Hand feel like Photoshop's: open hand at rest, closed while you drag, the picture glued to the pointer?
Is the end of the bar the right home for it in a picture window as well as in Design?
With the Hand in hand, does anything on the canvas react when it should not?
Should the Hand keep what you had picked (it does now, as Photoshop does)?
rough: The mock prints Hand (H); here the Hand has no key yet because H is Highlight. That is decision card a-hand-tool-pans-the-canvas-from-the-tool-bar-which-tool-should-the-h-key-pick.
The mock draws a Zoom tool after the Hand; it is left out because zoom is not a tool (your call on 2026-09-29).
A picture that already fits the window has nowhere to go, so a Hand drag there does nothing, the same as Photoshop at Fit.
Space does not borrow the Hand while held, because Space plays and pauses here; the only temporary pan is still two finger scrolling.
